screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article discussing drug interactions in epilepsy therapy, not a controlled clinical trial. No randomization or control groups mentioned.
This appears to be a case report describing a single patient's experience with dexamethasone-phenytoin interaction. Not a randomized controlled trial.

Randomized controlled study with 200 patients allocated to two groups: one receiving phenytoin and one not receiving phenytoin (observation control). Open-label design but meets criteria for random allocation with observation control.
Described as a prospective study evaluating risk of postoperative seizures and feasibility of early discontinuation of AED therapy. No mention of randomization or control groups.
This is a practice parameter/guideline document from the American Academy of Neurology, not a clinical trial. It reviews existing evidence but does not present original trial data.
Observational study of 100 patients in a therapy protocol. Patients were studied based on whether they received prophylactic anticonvulsants or not, but no randomization is described.
Explicitly described as a retrospective study of 68 patients. No randomization; patients were divided into those who received prophylactic anticonvulsants (33) and those who did not (38).

Double-blind trial of phenytoin therapy following craniotomy. The study design implies randomization and a control group (likely placebo given the double-blind nature). Significant reduction in epilepsy frequency observed in the active drug group.

Randomized controlled trial involving 284 patients with brain metastases. Patients were randomized to receive diazepam or no diazepam (observation control). Clear comparison between treatment and control groups.
Single-arm study analyzing 150 patients receiving oxcarbazepine. No control group or randomization described. Preliminary experience report rather than a controlled trial.
Commentary/letter to the editor discussing dexamethasone-phenytoin interactions. References other studies but is not itself a clinical trial.
Double-blind trial with 101 patients receiving phenytoin and 102 receiving placebo. Clear randomization and placebo control group. Epilepsy rates: 7.9% in phenytoin group vs 16.7% in placebo group.

Review article discussing mechanisms of epilepsy in brain tumor patients and medical treatment approaches. States that medical treatment has mainly been studied retrospectively. Not a primary clinical trial.
Prospective randomized series of glioma patients. Diazepam reduced seizure incidence from 16% to 2%. Randomized design with control group (no diazepam).
Randomized controlled trial with 189 patients receiving phenytoin and 185 patients receiving placebo under identical conditions. Clear randomization and placebo control.

Retrospective analysis of 35 patients divided into two groups based on whether they received postoperative radiation therapy. No randomization described; focus is on radiation therapy outcomes, not seizure prophylaxis.
Survey study of 197 practitioners exploring current practice patterns. Not a clinical trial; no randomization or control groups.
Survey of neurosurgeons (386 respondents) evaluating practice patterns. Not a clinical trial; no randomization or control groups.

Prospective randomized unblinded study of 100 newly diagnosed brain tumor patients. Patients randomized to receive anticonvulsants (AC Group, n=46) or not (No AC Group, n=54). Meets criteria for random allocation with observation control.
Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (1966-2004). This is a secondary analysis combining data from 5 primary trials, not a primary clinical trial itself.
Review article providing guidelines for family physicians. Uses illustrative clinical cases and literature review. Not a clinical trial.

Randomized trial comparing two different loading doses of phenytoin (10 mg/kg vs 15 mg/kg). Both groups received active treatment; no placebo or observation control group. Does not meet the criterion requiring placebo or observation in control groups.
Meta-analysis reviewing 30 publications and evaluating 6 controlled studies. This is a secondary analysis, not a primary clinical trial.
Observational study of 234 consecutive patients attending an outpatient clinic. No randomization; descriptive analysis of seizure presentation and incidence.
Retrospective analysis of 195 patients with intracerebral metastases. Patients were divided based on whether they received prophylactic anticonvulsants, but no randomization described.
Study of 128 patients where 41 were given prophylactic AEDs and 22 were not treated among those without preoperative seizures. No randomization described; appears to be non-randomized allocation.
Review article examining existing data on four topics related to anticonvulsant prophylaxis. Not a primary clinical trial.
Retrospective review of 538 patients undergoing elective craniotomy, focusing on 23 patients who had seizures within 24 hours. No randomization or control groups.
Retrospective review of charts of 65 consecutive adult patients with malignant gliomas. No randomization; descriptive analysis of seizure occurrence and anticonvulsant use.

Randomized double-blind trial comparing phenytoin vs sodium valproate. Both groups received active treatment; no placebo or observation control group. Does not meet the criterion requiring placebo or observation in control groups.

Retrospective series of 81 patients with brain metastasis from melanoma. Patients grouped by treatment approach but no randomization described. Focus is on survival outcomes, not primarily seizure prophylaxis.

Randomized trial of 276 patients allocated to carbamazepine, phenytoin, or no treatment. The 'no treatment' arm serves as an observation control group. Meets criteria for random allocation with observation control.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 74 patients with newly diagnosed brain tumors. Patients randomized to divalproex sodium or placebo. Clearly meets all selection criteria.
